name: V374 Pegasi
description: A star 0.34 solar radii and 0.28 solar masses that turns once in 10.7 hours; its magnetic field has been mapped.

radius.source: Morin et al., arXiv:0711.1418, Sect. 7: radius 0.34 solar radii (R sin i = 0.32 +/- 0.01, R ~ 0.34 for i ~ 70 deg (Sect. 7))

mass.source: Morin et al., arXiv:0711.1418, Sect. 7: mass 0.28 solar masses (0.28 +/- 0.05 from M_K (Sect. 7))

temperature.source: TESS Input Catalog 8.2 (VizieR IV/39/tic82), TIC 283410775: Teff

spin.source: Morin et al., arXiv:0711.1418, Sect. 7: rotation period 0.4456 d and an axis 70 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with

color.reason: The Washington Double Star catalogue (Mason et al. 2001, AJ 122, 3466; VizieR B/wds/wds) lists WDS 22012+2818 RAO 691: 0.3 arcsec apart, magnitudes 10 and 11.9: the companion gives 14.8% of the light, which a measured spectrum would blend with the star's. The color is the Planck spectrum at the star's temperature

text.card: A star 34% of the Sun's width that turns once in 10.7 hours, with a mapped magnetic field.
text.introduction: Morin et al. give it 0.34 solar radii, 0.28 solar masses, a rotation period of 10.7 hours and an axis tilted 70° from the line of sight.
